facts.text: Aitkin was named after William Alexander Aitken, a partner of the American Fur Company who led regional operations in the early 1800s.
Aitkin was founded in 1870 when the Northern Pacific Railroad was extended to that point, replacing and annexing Lexington.
Aitkin is a historic riverboat town on the Mississippi River in northern Minnesota.
Five Aitkin sites—Patrick Casey House, Potter/Casey Building, Carnegie Library, Northern Pacific Depot, and the County Courthouse—are on the National Register.
Aitkin has faced Mississippi River floods, with a 1950 flood reaching over 20 feet and a 2012 flood nearly 19 feet that even flooded lake cabins.
Today, tourism and service industries dominate Aitkin, supported by health care, education, human services, nonprofits, and hospitality.
